title: Inside the Bronze Brain of the Antikythera

segments.text: How did a hand‑crank move the heavens?
The mechanism contains thirty‑five bronze gears, though only thirty are clearly visible in the surviving fragments.
The biggest wheel is about 13 cm across with 223 teeth.
Turning the original hand crank would have driven this crown gear, moving the date pointer and all other dials together.
The gear train allowed the device to follow the motions of the Moon and the Sun through the zodiac, to predict eclipses and to model the Moon’s irregular orbit.
So a hand‑crank moves the heavens.
